title: Carrier, 10 mm M2.5 grid
summary: Every bought part sits on a small printed carrier: a 1.6 plate of whole 10 mm grid units with M2.5 holes at its corners. A box floor offers the grid points a design uses, as self-tap bosses or nut traps; a 4 thick bench plate is the whole grid, for prototyping. A carrier never knows which it is on.

views.label: On the bench
views.caption: Drag the slider to set a 3 × 4 carrier down on a 6 × 6 bench plate: its four holes land on grid points, and M2.5 × 6 screws tap straight into the bench. The middle of the plate is opened to a frame; each hole keeps its grid cell solid.

views.label: In a box
views.caption: A piece of box floor with two 3 × 2 carriers. Left, the default: the carrier stands on Ø6 × 4 bosses and the screws tap into them, leaving 4 mm under it for wires. Right, the nut option: the carrier lies flat and the nuts sit in traps under the 2.4 floor. Cut it open to see the pilot holes and the traps.

views.label: Fit piece
views.caption: A 5 × 2 piece of bench plate with tap holes 1.9, 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 at 1 to 4 dots, and a Ø2.9 clearance hole at the end. Drive an M2.5 × 6 into each: the right hole takes a thread firmly without splitting.

checks: Does an M2.5 × 6 drive in with a screwdriver, cutting a thread rather than forcing one?
Does the head pull down firm, and stay firm after taking it out and back in twice?
Does the plate stay whole round the hole, no split, no bulge underneath?
Does a screw drop through the Ø2.9 hole?
fit.print: Print base down, no supports, in the enclosure's material (PETG).
